Use Tier 2: replace the candidate-independent history pooling with a candidate-conditioned attention readout within the existing network. The latest macro HR@10 of 0.4775 trails the baseline’s 0.505, with Electronics falling from 0.420 to 0.305, making representation quality a stronger target than further optimizer tuning. Compressing every history into one vector may discard interests relevant to individual candidates; this is a hypothesis to test, not an established diagnosis.

The primary component is model_design: let each candidate’s shared item embedding query the causally contextualized history through learned low-dimensional query and key projections. Mask padding, retain the existing learned recency penalty, and use the attention weights to produce a separate history representation for each candidate. Replace the existing pooling and scoring readout with one shared scoring network that consumes this representation, the last contextual state, and the candidate embedding. Train all components jointly using the existing binary logistic objective, keeping prefix sampling, negative sampling, backbone, and optimizer settings fixed to isolate the readout change.

The supporting component is training_evaluation: select one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10, and update the predictor writer to instantiate this same architecture and scoring path. Retain all four category routes, supplied splits, training seed 42, and the pinned validation protocol with 200 users and 99 unique negatives per category. Use low-dimensional attention projections and candidate chunking to control single-GPU memory, and assess the change through host-evaluated macro HR@10 and category results. Every prediction will come from exactly one jointly trained model per category, with no auxiliary fitted scores or checkpoint averaging.
